injuries.shortComment: Hutchins (knee) was placed on injured reserve Friday.
injuries.longComment: Hutchins appeared in both of the Patriots' first two games of the 2026 campaign, accumulating three total tackles. The rookie will now miss at least four games while tending to a knee injury. While Hutchins has played sparingly, his absence will still allow Gabe Jacas and Jose Ramirez to see a little more action.

injuries.shortComment: Gilliam (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
injuries.longComment: Gilliam was limited in all three Week 3 practice sessions. The fullback sustained a knee injury during the Patriots' Week 2 win over the Steelers, but it won't stop the 29-year-old from suiting up for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Gilliam has seen 33 offensive snaps and 26 special-teams snaps through two games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: The Patriots placed Pettus (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Pettus exited the second quarter of Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers with an ankle injury, and he'll now have to miss at least the next four games while on IR. With Craig Woodson (shoulder) also injured, the team will likely look to sign or elevate a player from the practice squad  for Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: The Patriots opened the 21-day practice window for Schooler (back) on Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Schooler can now return to practice but won't be eligible to appear in a game until Week 5 due to being on the reserve/non-football injury list. Once officially activated, the 29-year-old should contribute as a depth defender.

injuries.shortComment: Davis (neck) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Davis was unavailable for the team's Week 2 win over the Steelers as a result of a neck injury, but he now appears to be healthy ahead of Sunday's contest against the Jaguars. The 29-year-old will slot in as a starting cornerback versus Jacksonville.

injuries.shortComment: Williams caught one of two targets for 10 yards in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Despite A.J. Brown (ankle) missing his first game after going down in Week 1 against Seattle, Williams played just 20 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Pittsburgh. He operated as the fourth receiver, well behind Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs and slot man DeMario Douglas. Williams doesn't hold much fantasy value in redraft formats.

injuries.shortComment: Spillane logged six tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Spillane played 100 percent of the Patriots' 70 defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The inside linebacker has now played all 120 of the team's defensive snaps through two regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Woods logged 10 tackles (eight solo) and defensed one pass in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Woods played 86 percent of the Patriots' defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The cornerback started in place of Carlton Davis (neck), and he'll likely do so again in Week 3 against the Jaguars if the latter remains absent.

injuries.shortComment: Ponder logged five tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and recovered a fumble he returned for a touchdown in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Ponder recovered an Aaron Rodgers fumble and took it 19 yards for a touchdown to extend the Patriots' 13-3 lead to the game-winning 20-3 score. The outside linebacker played 77 percent of the team's defensive snaps in the contest.

injuries.shortComment: Elliss logged 12 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, and forced a fumble in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Elliss led all players in Sunday's contest in tackles. The inside linebacker played all 70 defensive snaps in the contest and has missed just one defensive snap through two regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: The Patriots placed Onwenu (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle in the Patriots' win over the Steelers on Sunday, and he appears likely to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Greg Van Roten is likely the next man up at right guard for New England.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a 20-3 win over the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Douglas not only posted an unimpactful stat line, he also was on the field for only 47 percent of New England's offensive snaps after logging a a 62 percent snap share Week 1. Both Mack Hollins (71 percent) and Romeo Doubs (67 percent) recorded a significantly higher offensive snap share Week 2, though Douglas remained ahead of Kyle Williams (20 percent) and Efton Chism (18 percent). With only six catches (on nine targets) for 29 yards through two contests, Douglas has yet to give fantasy managers any confidence in deploying him in lineups.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson caught all eight of his targets for 53 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: The veteran tight end continues to have an impressive start to the season, hauling in TD strikes of one and two yards from Tyler Shough. but Johnson had a tough end to his day as he fumbled to end the Saints' final possession while they were trying to mount a comeback late in the fourth quarter. Johnson has put together a 15-173-3 line on 19 targets through three games, and he'll look to atone for his miscue in a Week 4 home tilt against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Kamara carried the ball nine times for 36 yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: The veteran RB once again took a back seat to Travis Etienne to begin the game, but that changed after the former Jaguar aggravated a hamstring strain and left the game in the third quarter. Over the Saints' last five possessions, Kamara split the workload in the backfield with Kendre Miller, getting six touches to Miller's five. The severity of Etienne's injury isn't yet clear, but if he misses significant time, Kamara and Miller would likely continue working in tandem, with rookie CJ Donaldson also potentially mixing in as a short-yardage option.

injuries.shortComment: Shough completed 29 of 42 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders. He added 36 rushing yards on his lone carry, but also lost two fumbles.
injuries.longComment: The second-year QB was dynamic once again, tossing two TDs each to tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, but protection issues in the absence of left tackle Kelvin Banks (ankle) ending up proving costly as all four of the Saints' fourth-quarter possessions ended in turnovers, causing them to squander a 27-22 lead. Shough has thrown eight touchdowns through three games but has also given the ball away six times (three INTs and three lost fumbles), and he'll try to clean up those issues in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Olave caught nine of 13 targets for 107 yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards, but all four of Tyler Shough's TD passes went to tight ends instead of Olave. Olave has hauled in more than 100 yards in two of three games to begin the season, amassing a 27-375-1 line on 36 targets, and he'll look to keep rolling in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

injuries.shortComment: Etienne exited Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders due to an injury to the same hamstring which bothered him in practice leading up to the game, head coach Kellen Moore revealed after the loss, John Hendrix of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: Etienne's second-half hamstring injury was an aggravation of a previous injury, which limited his practice participation Wednesday and Thursday. Soft-tissue injuries have a tendency to linger, so it wouldn't be surprising if Etienne missed some game action to allow his hamstring to heal, especially since the Saints could opt for a cautious approach with Etienne after signing him to a four-year, $52 million contract in March. Further testing on the injury may be required before a return timetable is established, though Moore said that an update on Etienne and other injured players may be provided Monday. If Etienne were to miss any time, more touches would be available for Alvin Kamara, CJ Donaldson and Kendre Miller.

injuries.shortComment: Jennings has a knee injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: The linebacker recorded three tackles (two solo) and a pass breakup before exiting. Jennings played more on special teams than defense in New Orleans' first two games.

injuries.shortComment: Granderson (ankle) has returned to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.longComment: Granderson was briefly sidelined with an ankle injury that he suffered in the third quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 29-year-old is back in his starting role as a weakside linebacker for New Orleans.

injuries.shortComment: Werner (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
injuries.longComment: Werner suffered a stinger in the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Isaiah Stalbird and Danny Stutsman are two candidates to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker.

injuries.shortComment: Emerson (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: Emerson injured his shoulder during the Saints' Week 2 win over the Ravens. He drew the questionable tag for Week 3 following a limited practice Friday, but he'll be sidelined for Sunday's game after failing to be cleared by medical staff following pregame warmups. Jayden Price, Michael Reid and Decamerion Richardson will provide depth in the secondary in Emerson's absence.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: For a third consecutive week, Wilson will be the Saints' emergency QB3, meaning he cannot play Sunday unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: The Saints elevated Moreno-Cropper from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: Moreno-Cropper is set for his first taste of regular-season action in 2026. The wide receiver is being elevated alongside Kevin Austin to supplement a Saints wide receiver corps now without Barion Brown (hamstring). With Week 3 marking Austin's third practice squad elevation, the Saints will be unable to utilize him in the future without signing him to the active roster. This predicament means Moreno-Cropper may be the go-to wide receiver elevation for Week 4 and Week 5 if the team likes his game-day performance in Week 3.

injuries.shortComment: The Saints elevated Austin from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: Austin has been elevated for a third consecutive week, meaning the Saints have elected to exhaust the wide receiver's final practice squad elevation just three weeks into the 2026 regular season. Austin has logged 10 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps over his two contests, catching his only target for seven yards.

injuries.shortComment: Banks (ankle) underwent surgery this week, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: While head coach Kellen Moore indicated that the procedure went well, Banks will remain on injured reserve for the foreseeable future. As a result, Mason Murphy should continue to be more involved.

injuries.shortComment: Miller (illness) doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: Miller was under the weather Thursday, keeping him off the practice field. However, he was a full participant Friday. Miller was a healthy scratch for the 24-17 win over Baltimore in Week 2, meaning he is in danger of suffering the same fate versus Las Vegas, though his services may be needed on special teams with WR Barion Brown (hamstring) ruled out. With that in mind, if Miller is inactive, that would likely mean more work for Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson behind Travis Etienne.

injuries.shortComment: Sanker (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: Sanker had limited practice participation Wednesday seemingly as a precautionary measure, and his return to a full session Thursday puts the second-year defensive back on track to play Sunday against Las Vegas. Sanker has 13 tackles (10 solo) through two regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Young (calf) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: Young opened Week 3 prep as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, but his full session Thursday puts the seventh-year pass rusher on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Young has two tackles (one solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through the first two games of the regular season.

injuries.shortComment: Stalbird (shoulder) was a full participant at the Saints' practice Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Stalbird was unavailable for the team's 24-17 win over the Ravens in Week 2 due to a shoulder injury, but he now appears to be back to full health. The 26-year-old will be back in his role as a top depth option behind Kaden Elliss and Pete Werner at inside linebacker Sunday versus the Raiders.

injuries.shortComment: Delp gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 24-17 victory over the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Delp didn't suit up for the 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit in Week 1 due to a hamstring issue, though he was on the field for Sunday's 24-17 upset win over Baltimore. However, despite the rookie's availability in Week 2, he appeared in just nine of the Saints' 68 offensive snaps, catching his only target for eight yards, while logging six snaps on special teams. Although Delp could see more action moving ahead, it doesn't appear as if he will be more involved than Noah Fant and Juwan Johnson anytime soon.

injuries.shortComment: Lance caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 24-17 victory against Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: Lance was on the field for 54 of New Orleans' 68 offensive snaps, but he had only one pass thrown his way by Tyler Shough. Chris Olave (10 targets) and Devaughn Vele (seven) got 17 of the Saints' 19 total wideout targets, so Lance wasn't alone in having a quiet day among the team's complementary options. Barion Brown logged just two offensive snaps Sunday and Kevin Austin notched five, so Lance seems to be clearly ahead of both in the pecking order.

injuries.shortComment: Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Neither team could generate that much offense in tough conditions Sunday, but Zvada helped the Giants build and maintain their lead with four field goals, all of which came from within 40 yards. The rookie kicker has made all six of his field-goal attempts and each of his four extra-point tries through the first three games of the regular season.

injuries.shortComment: Winston completed 14 of 22 passes for 118 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over Tennessee. He added 14 rushing yards on two carries.
injuries.longComment: The 32-year-old quarterback was getting his first start in place of Jaxson Dart (knee), but Winston wasn't asked to do very much as the Giants leaned on their backfield and their defense. To his credit, Winston did avoid committing any turnovers, which may be all coach John Harbaugh needs from him. Winston will look for opportunities to be more productive at home in Week 4 against the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Nabers caught five of six targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: The Giants' passing game struggled with Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), and while Nabers led the team in catches and targets, he didn't make much of an impact -- his longest gain went for just 12 yards. That doesn't bode well for the rest of the third-year wideout's campaign with Dart not expected back until 2027, but Nabers and Winston will have plenty of time to develop more chemistry. Nabers will take a 12-96-0 line on 19 targets into a Week 4 home tilt against the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Skattebo carried the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught three of four targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: With Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), the Giants leaned a little more heavily on their backfield and Skattebo saw a season high in touches while hitting for 100-plus scrimmage yards for the first time in 2026. The second-year back's longest play came on a 30-yard toss in the first quarter, as he made himself available downfield to bail out a scrambling Winston. Through three games, Skattebo is showing no ill effects from the ankle injury that ended his rookie campaign early, and he's collected 177 rushing yards and a TD on 50 carries while adding a 7-59-0 line on eight targets. He figures to see a big workload again in Week 4 at home against the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Burns will undergo an MRI for a right knee injury that he sustained during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.longComment: Burns had to be carted off the field after sustaining a right knee injury during he second half of Sunday's game. He's scheduled for an MRI later this evening, at which point the Giants will have a better sense of the recovery timeline for the veteran pass rusher. Kayvon Thibodeaux would be in line for a larger role defensively if Burns were to miss time.

injuries.shortComment: Banks (calf) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Banks practiced in a limited capacity leading into Week 3, but will miss his second straight game due to a calf injury. Colton Hood should see more playing time in his absence.

injuries.shortComment: Nubin (calf) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Nubin was a limited participant in practice every day leading into Week 3. With the 25-year-old out, both Ar'Darius Washington and Jason Pinnock are in line for larger roles against Tennessee.

injuries.shortComment: Singletary (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Singletary had little impact in Week 2, rushing just three times for nine yards amongst a busy backfield. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as complementary options behind Cam Skattebo against Tennessee.

injuries.shortComment: With Tyler Nubin (calf) inactive, Washington will start at safety against the Titans on Sunday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Nubin was not cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so Washington and Jevon Holland will be the Giants' starting safeties for Week 3, with Jason Pinnock and Elijah Campbell providing depth at the position. Washington has two tackles (one solo) through two regular-season games, and the last time he was a regular starter on defense was during the second half of the 2024 campaign as a member of the Ravens.

injuries.shortComment: The Giants elevated Berrios from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: The Giants have elected to expend Berrios' last practice squad elevation, calling upon the wide receiver for three consecutive weeks. The 30-year-old remains the team's primary kick and punt returner, receiving no targets but recording 81 kick-return yards over the past two games. Berrios will need to be signed to the active roster to participate in any more regular-season games for the Giants after Week 3.

injuries.shortComment: The Giants signed Haener from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: In the wake of Jaxson Dart's serious left knee injury that will sideline him for the rest of the regular season, Jameis Winston will get the first chance to be New York's starting QB on Sunday against the Titans, and Haener's standing as the only other signal-caller on the roster implied that he'd serve as the backup in the initial contest without Dart. Whether or not that'll last beyond Week 3 remains to be seen, but Haener does have NFL experience under his belt, as he completed 18 of 39 passes for 226 yards, one touchdown and one interception and rushed 11 times for 22 yards in eight appearances (one start) as a member of the Saints in 2024.

injuries.shortComment: Thomas (groin) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: Thomas was limited in Wednesday's practice before logging a DNP on Thursday. The left tackle upgraded to a limited participant once again Friday, managing to avoid any injury designation for Sunday's contest. Thomas will be protecting Jameis Winston's blind side due to the injury to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee).

injuries.shortComment: The Giants officially placed Dart (knee) on injured reserve Thursday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: This transaction was inevitable after it was revealed Dart will miss the rest of the regular season due to damage to the MCL, PCL and meniscus that he suffered in his left knee during the Giants' Week 2 loss to the Rams. Fortunately for Dart, his ACL is intact, and head coach John Harbaugh also told Connor Hughes of SNY.tv on Wednesday that the second-year quarterback may be able to return in the postseason, if the team qualifies. In the meantime, Jameis Winston will cover QB duties for the Giants.

injuries.shortComment: McFadden (neck) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice estimate,  Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: McFadden missed the Giants' Week 2 loss to the Rams due to a neck injury. The linebacker was not able to log more than a limited practice session during Week 2 prep, a benchmark McFadden has already surpassed with his estimate of full participation Wednesday. Absent any setbacks, the 26-year-old should be healthy enough to suit up for Sunday's game against the Titans.

injuries.shortComment: Edmunds logged five assisted tackles and one pass defensed in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Edmunds did not record a solo tackle in Sunday's contest but assisted on five takedowns. The linebacker played 100 percent of the Giants' defensive snaps for the second consecutive week, now having been on the field for all 118 defensive plays this season.

injuries.shortComment: Holland logged eight tackles (five solo), one pass defensed for an interception and one fumble recovery in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Holland tied Tyler Nubin for the most Giants tackles in Monday's loss. The free safety picked off reigning MVP Matthew Stafford in the second quarter of the game as the Giants tried to mount a comeback. Holland also helped force and recovered a Kyren Williams fumble at the Rams' 11-yard line late in the first half, setting up the first of two field goals that constituted New York's scoring Monday night.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson played 16 of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps but did not haul in any of his four targets during Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: All four of Johnson's targets came in the first half, three of which were in the opening quarter. The third-year tight end failed to record a catch, but he did log a tackle on Trent McDuffie after the latter intercepted Jameis Winston midway through the second quarter. Johnson is firmly behind Isaiah Likely on the depth chart, though all of the Giants pass catchers figure to see their production dip with Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart, the latter of whom could miss the rest of the season due to a knee injury.

injuries.shortComment: Beckham played three of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps and did not see a target in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Beckham has logged only 14 snaps on offense without recording a target through the first two games of the regular season. Despite the lack of usage, the veteran wide receiver could factor more into the Giants' gameplan moving forward if Malik Nabers were to miss time due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during Monday's loss. The Giants will head back MetLife Stadium to host the Titans on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Mooney caught two of three targets for 48 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Mooney led the team with 48 receiving yards in what was a disappointing outing for New York's offense. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury on the first possession of the game, and he is expected to be sidelined for the foreseeable future. Mooney will look to continue to build chemistry with new starter Jameis Winston in Week 3 against the Titans.

injuries.shortComment: Harris turned four carries into six yards during the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Harris was a healthy scratch for Week 1 against the Cowboys, but the sixth-year pro suited up for Monday's loss. He ended up playing eight offensive snaps, well behind Cam Skattebo (34) and Devin Singletary (15), though noticeably ahead of Tyrone Tracy (one). Two of Harris' carries also came in the red zone. He figures to be the Giants' RB3 for the time being, but with Jaxson Dart (knee) potentially done for the year, the team's running game will likely take on more importance heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Titans on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Sadiq caught seven of eight passes for 105 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The rookie tight end made a spectacular play to haul in his first career TD reception in the second quarter, leaping from about the five-yard line and stretching out the full length of his 6-foot-3 frame to bring in a 24-yard pass from Geno Smith. Sadiq is very quickly making an impact with his athleticism, and through his first three NFL games he's compiled a 12-143-1 line on 14 targets while adding a three-yard score on his only carry. He'll look to continue building chemistry with Smith in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.shortComment: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries and threw a two-point conversion.
injuries.longComment: The veteran QB was nearly flawless as the Jets nearly pulled off the upset, with his only turnover being a fumble on his fifth sack of the day late in the fourth quarter, ending his final possession. Smith spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different targets and connecting with Garrett Wilson, Jeremy Ruckert and rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq for his scores. Smith has been extremely efficient to begin the season, posting a 75.5 percent completion rate (77-for-102) with a 4:0 TD:INT and 7.7 YPA. He'll look to stay sharp in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson caught 10 of 13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to Detroit.
injuries.longComment: The star wideout paced Jets pass catchers in all three receiving categories, and his 23-yard TD from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter tied the game at 24-24, only for the Lions to respond inside the final two minutes. It's Wilson's first 100-yard performance since Week 14 of the 2024 season, as injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign. Wilson has also found the end zone in back-to-back games, and he'll take a 21-243-2 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.shortComment: Hall (thigh) outlined that he "felt something" when running before departing Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Hall was forced out of the game in the fourth quarter after sustaining a leg injury while being tackled. The running back was unable to return to the contest, and he will likely undergo additional imaging to determine the severity of the injury. If he is forced to miss any action moving forward, Braelon Allen would stand to operate as the team's No. 1 option in the backfield.

injuries.shortComment: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Parham was carted off the field after sustaining a knee injury and will not return. Jordan Meredith will take over at left guard for the rest of Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Stiggers (hand) returned to Sunday's game versus the Lions, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Stiggers exited the contest after suffering a hand injury early in the first quarter. However, it appears the injury wasn't anything serious, though his return mostly impacts the special-teams unit while adding depth to the secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Ossai (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Ossai was trending in the right direction for Week 3 after logging a full practice Friday, and the veteran pass rusher has been given the green light to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. It will be Ossai's 2026 regular-season debut, and he's expected to serve in a rotational role at defensive end behind starters Will McDonald and Kingsley Enagbare.

injuries.shortComment: Wright (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Wright has been limited to special-teams work through the first two games of the regular season, and he'll be a healthy scratch for Week 3 while rookie D'Angelo Ponds suits up. Wright's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Bears on Sunday, Oct. 4, though there doesn't appear to be a clear path to playing time for the sixth-year pro.

injuries.shortComment: Grupe (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The Jets have decided to elevate Jason Sanders from the practice squad, leaving Grupe inactive for the third consecutive week. Grupe doesn't currently appear to have a clear path to taking over placekicking duties at the moment, although that could change if Sanders begins to struggle.

injuries.shortComment: Mitchell (finger) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Mitchell was listed as questionable for Week 3 after sustaining a finger injury last week, and it turns out he is not ready to take the field Sunday. Mitchell -- who garnered 12 targets last week -- joins fellow pass catchers Omar Cooper (ankle) and Mason Taylor (thumb) on the sidelines, so Kenyon Sadiq and Isaiah Williams figure to see some extra opportunities behind top option Garrett Wilson.

injuries.shortComment: Nwangwu (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Nwangwu was listed as doubtful for Sunday's contest after Friday's practice. The Jets' kick returner had an outside chance to suit up Sunday despite not logging a single day of practice throughout Week 3 prep. After a Saturday examination, it's been determined that Nwangwu will not be ready for the game, leaving Isaiah Williams as the primary kick and punt returner for the Jets' showdown with the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: The Jets signed Pritchett from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: The Jets signed Pritchett to the practice squad Sept. 2 after waiving the wide receiver on cutdown day. The second-year player out of South Alabama has yet to play in an NFL contest. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) cannot suit up for Sunday's game against the Lions, Pritchett is set to be the No. 4 option for the Jets in his debut.

injuries.shortComment: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Shepard is set to suit up as the No. 6 wide receiver for the Jets in Sunday's game against the Lions. The new practice squad face was elevated for a scenario where Adonai Mitchell (finger) is unable to play in Sunday's contest. If Mitchell receives the green light, Shepard may spend his first elevation with the team inactive.

injuries.shortComment: The Jets elevated Sanders from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Sanders will once again be the Jets' primary kicker for the third consecutive week and is set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Lions. The 30-year-old has now seen all three of his practice squad elevations expended, meaning he will need to be signed to the Jets' active roster to kick for the team in Week 4 against the Bears.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (knee) underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn ACL and will miss the rest of the season, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.longComment: Smith suffered a knee injury during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He will finish the 2026 campaign without a catch (one target), adding four carries for 13 yards. With Smith, Omar Cooper (ankle) and Tim Patrick (groin) out of the equation, Isaiah Williams could be in line for more opportunities behind Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson. The Jets also signed Malik McClain off the practice squad Tuesday, which will help fill some of the void left by the injuries within the receiving corps.

injuries.shortComment: Onyemata (groin) underwent core-muscle surgery Wednesday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
injuries.longComment: Onyemata was injured during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He was placed on the injured reserve list Tuesday, and while that means he will miss at least four games, he is anticipated to be out longer, though head coach Aaron Glenn expects him back before the end of the season. While Onyemata is out of commission, Darrell Jackson, Jowon Briggs, T'Vondre Sweat and Harrison Phillips will presumably see more snaps in each game moving ahead.

injuries.shortComment: Davis posted four tackles (three solo) during the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Davis was one of six Jets players to play all 59 defensive snaps during Sunday's OT loss. The veteran linebacker is up to 12 total tackles through two games and on pace to crack 100 tackles for a 10th straight year and the 13th time in his NFL career. He should stay busy Week 3 against the Lions on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Sherwood posted six tackles (three solo) and a pass defense during the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Sherwood was working through a minor knee issue during Week 2 prep, but he managed to play every single defensive snap during Sunday's OT loss and finished tied with Dane Belton for the most tackles on the Jets. Sherwood is up to 10 total tackles through two games, and he's currently behind pace to reach the 100-tackle mark for a third consecutive year. He'll have his hands full in the Jets' Week 3 road tilt against the Lions on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: The Jets signed Reeder off the practice squad Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Reeder played 25 snaps on special teams as a standard elevation in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers. He's now got a spot on the 53-man roster and will serve as a depth linebacker and special-teams piece for Gang Green.

injuries.shortComment: Davis didn't have any output in the box score during the Jets' overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Davis didn't see any playing time on offense for the second straight week, as Breece Hall and Braelon Allen once again handled the ground attack. While the 24-year-old did manage to record a tackle across his 22 special-teams snaps, he will likely continue to serve in a limited role unless Hall or Allen gets hurt.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Johnson appeared on Saturday's injury report as a DNP with a knee injury. The sudden appearance of the injury granted the reserve offensive lineman virtually no time to recover, and he will be unable to suit up for Monday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Greenard (pectoral) is listed as questionable ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Greenard was a full participant in Saturday's practice, marking the first time the linebacker has achieved that level of participation since sustaining his pectoral injury. Despite practicing in full, Greenard remains questionable to suit up for Monday's contest as the team makes certain the 29-year-old is ready for the challenge.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Brown suffered an ankle injury during Week 3 prep and has been unable to practice since sustaining the injury. The wide receiver will officially not be suiting up for Monday's game, leaving Darius Cooper to be the No. 4 wide receiver behind DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon.

injuries.shortComment: Shipley (foot) was a limited participant in Saturday's practice but does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Shipley ended the week with back-to-back limited practices while working through a foot injury, but he's been officially cleared to play for MNF. Saquon Barkley (shoulder) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen) have also been cleared to play, so Shipley will serve as the Eagles' third option out of the backfield.

injuries.shortComment: Bigsby (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Bigsby was working through an abdominal injury throughout the week, but he faded an injury tag after logging a full practice Saturday. He worked in an elevated role on offense against the Titans in Week 2, but Bigsby will be the Eagles' RB2 for Monday after Saquon Barkley was able to overcome a shoulder stinger. Will Shipley (foot) will serve as the third option out of the backfield.

injuries.shortComment: Goedert (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears.
injuries.longComment: Goedert was unable to practice all week due to an MCL sprain that he sustained during the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. Zach Ertz was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, and he figures to be elevated to the active roster for Monday's game and provide depth at tight end behind Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins. Goedert's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 4, though he should be considered week-to-week.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (hamstring) is participating in Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
injuries.longComment: Smith has been working through a hamstring injury, which prevented him from practicing Thursday before he returned for Friday's session in a limited capacity. His status for Monday night's game against the Bears will be more clear once the Eagles announce their injury designations following Saturday's practice. Smith is coming off a 10-117-1 receiving line (on 13 targets) against the Titans in Week 2, and if he were to be ruled out or limited against Chicago, then Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would all be in line for more targets from Jalen Hurts.

injuries.shortComment: Mukuba (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Mukuba was a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited in Thursday's session. The safety appears to be over the knee injury that plagued him throughout Week 2. Mukuba will likely head into Monday night's game against the Bears healthy and without any injury designation.

injuries.shortComment: Carter (wrist) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Carter logged a limited practice session Thursday before upgrading to full participation Friday. The defensive tackle appears to be over the wrist injury that he played through in the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. There is a strong chance Carter heads into Monday night's matchup with the Bears fully healthy and clear of any injury designation.

injuries.shortComment: Barkley (stinger) was a full practice participant Friday.
injuries.longComment: Barkley's status for Week 3 was chief among the health concerns coming out of a Week 2 win at Tennessee in which he suffered a stinger and missed most of the first half. After kicking off this week with a limited practice Thursday, he handled every practice rep one day later, indicating he's good to go for Monday's contest in Chicago. Having said that, Barkley told Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia on Friday that he'll wear protective gear around his neck and shoulders this week and perhaps as long as symptoms of the stinger are impacting him.

injuries.shortComment: Cooper caught two of three targets for 26 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: With Dallas Goedert (knee) going down early in the game, Cooper played 31 offensive snaps as the No. 4 receiver after logging just eight in Week 1 against the Commanders. Cooper responded to the increased playing time by breaking free in the back of the end zone with nine seconds left in the fourth quarter to catch the game-winning three-yard touchdown from Jalen Hurts. Cooper doesn't carry much value in redraft fantasy leagues and would need an injury or two ahead of him at the position for that to change.

injuries.shortComment: Mundt caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-20 win against the Titans.
injuries.longComment: Mundt started along with fellow tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and he logged 49 of Philadelphia's 76 offensive snaps. The significant playing time was partly due to Goedert exiting in the first half after spraining his MCL. Goedert is now slated to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, but that won't necessarily mean that Mundt will be an attractive fantasy waiver-wire pickup. The Eagles signed veteran Zach Ertz to a contract Tuesday, and he'll likely slide in as the team's top tight end during Goedert's absence, though it's unclear how long Ertz will need to get up to speed.

injuries.shortComment: Baun recorded four total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 24-20 win over Tennessee.
injuries.longComment: Baun matched his season low in tackles from the 2025 campaign Sunday, but he was still on the field for all 53 of the team's defensive snaps in the contest. He has now compiled 16 total tackles (nine solo) and two passes defensed over two games this season. The linebacker will likely be more involved against the Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 3.

injuries.shortComment: Campbell recorded 10 total tackles (six solo) and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: Campbell was able to notch double-digit takedowns for the first time this season, and he stripped running back Tyjae Spears in the second quarter, but the ball went out of bounds before it could be recovered. The linebacker has now compiled 19 total tackles (11 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a forced fumble over two games this year.

injuries.shortComment: Ertz signed with the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, Chris McPherson of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Monday that the 35-year-old Ertz would sign with the Eagles as a member of the practice squad, and that was confirmed a day later. Ertz, who won his lone Super Bowl ring and earned each of his three Pro Bowl nods as a member of the Eagles from 2013 through 2021, may need some time to get back up to full speed after tearing his ACL last December and then not participating in training camp with a team. Once he's fully ramped up, Ertz could settle in as the Eagles' top tight end with Dallas Goedert (knee) facing a multi-week absence and with Eli Stowers (quadriceps/hamstring) and Grant Calcaterra (back) already on injured reserve.

injuries.shortComment: Elliott converted his only field-goal attempt and made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: Elliott made the most of his lone field-goal try of the day, making a 58-yarder in the third quarter. The kicker hasn't been leaned on often so far this year, but he has made both of his field-goal tries, and Sunday's 58-yard make is rather inspiring after Elliott combined to make five of 15 attempts from 50-plus yards over the last two seasons.

injuries.shortComment: Lemon caught his lone target for 14 yards while turning one carry into minus-5 yards during the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Lemon recorded minus-5 receiving yards on three catches during his NFL debut against the Commanders in Week 1. He was at least able to stay in the positive against Tennessee with a 14-yard catch on the last play of the third quarter, which moved the chains on third-and-8 and led to a two-yard touchdown run by Tank Bigsby four plays later. Lemon saw his workload in training camp severely limited due to a hamstring injury, so it may take a few weeks for the rookie first-rounder to ramp up his production. That said, with Dallas Goedert set to miss multiple weeks due to a sprained MCL, Lemon could operate in an elevated role in the passing game, starting with the Eagles' Week 3 road tilt against the Bears on Monday, Sept. 28.

injuries.shortComment: Wicks caught five of six targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: While he wasn't able to get into the end zone, Wicks still had a strong showing as the Eagles' clear WR2 behind DeVonta Smith and ahead of rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. The former Packer is looking good in his new offense, producing a 7-147-1 line on 10 targets through two contests, and Wicks will look to keep developing chemistry with Jalen Hurts in a Week 3 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.shortComment: Hurts completed 26 of 37 passes for 264 yards and two touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 24-20 win over Tennessee. He added 16 yards on five carries.
injuries.longComment: Both picks led to points for the Titans, including a fourth-quarter field goal that put the home side up 20-17 with less than two minutes left. Hurts atoned for his mistakes, however, leading a nine-play, 65-yard drive that was capped by a three-yard TD strike to Darius Cooper that won the game. Hurts has already thrown five touchdowns in two games after tossing a career-high 25 in 16 regular-season contests in 2025, and he'll look to keep that momentum going in a Week 3 road trip to Chicago.

injuries.shortComment: Dalton is active as the Eagles' top backup quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
injuries.longComment: After facing competition from Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton for the No. 2 job behind Jalen Hurts throughout training camp and the preseason, Dalton has emerged as the victor in the job battle. Dalton will suit up for the second week in a row, while McKee is inactive as the emergency No. 3 quarterback and Payton is also donning street clothes.

injuries.shortComment: DeJean (calf) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Titans.
injuries.longComment: DeJean was working through both calf and abdominal injuries during Week 2 prep, but he finished with a DNP/LP/FP practice log, with Friday's full session being enough for the third-year pro to avoid an injury tag. DeJean played every single defensive snap during the Eagles' Week 1 win over the Commanders, finishing with eight tackles (four solo).

injuries.shortComment: Boswell made all three of his field-goal attempts and each of his three extra-point tries during the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Boswell missed one kick in each of the first two games of the regular season, but he was perfect during Sunday's win. He connected on field goals from 44, 36 and 33 yards, the last of which occurred just before the two-minute warning of the fourth quarter and gave Pittsburgh the lead for good. It appears the Steelers' offense may have figured something out in Week 3, and that continued success would raise Boswell's scoring floor over the coming weeks.

injuries.shortComment: Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 10 yards in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: After averaging just 5.2 yards per attempt while completing a sparse 59.5 percent of his passes over the first two games of the season, Rodgers begin clicking in Mike McCarthy's offense Sunday. The future Hall of Famer averaged 8.6 yards per attempt and had five completions of 22 yards or more while connecting with nine different pass catchers overall. Rodgers distributed the ball on his three touchdown passes as well, hitting Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and DK Metcalf from 38, 23 and six yards out, respectively. Rodgers' passing yardage total was a season high despite his completion total being his lowest through three games, and he'll look to carry the momentum into a Week 4 road matchup against an aggressive Browns defense on Thursday night.

injuries.shortComment: Metcalf brought in three of five targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Metcalf once again put together a very modest receiving line, but the veteran wideout managed to deliver his first touchdown of the season on a six-yard grab late in the third quarter. Metcalf's high-water mark through three games is the four-catch, 40-yard tally he managed in Week 1 against the Falcons, but with Aaron Rodgers and the passing attack as a whole looking much more cohesive Sunday, there's some hope for an uptick in production during a Week 4 road matchup against the Browns on Thursday night.

injuries.shortComment: Warren rushed 17 times for 127 yards and secured three of four targets for 49 yards in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Warren had the Steelers' backfield to himself Sunday due to the absence of Rico Dowdle (toe), and the former took full advantage. Filling his usual versatile role, Warren came within striking distance of his single-game career high of 143 rushing yards, and he would have easily blown by that figure had an 87-yard run just before the midway point of the fourth quarter not been nullified by a DK Metcalf holding penalty. If Dowdle is unable to beat the short turnaround for a Week 4 road matchup against the Browns on Thursday night, Warren will be in store for another hefty workload in the divisional clash.

injuries.shortComment: Echols is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bengals, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Echols took a hit to the head while on special teams but was able to walk off the field under his own power. He hasn't seen much playing time on defense this season, but if he can't return, then Daylen Everette and Doneiko Slaughter would be the primary depth options at cornerback.

injuries.shortComment: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: As the emergency third quarterback, Howard is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph were to be removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Rookie third-round quarterback Drew Allar (coach's decision) will be a healthy scratch for a third consecutive week.

injuries.shortComment: Dean (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against Cincinnati.
injuries.longComment: Dean was working through an ankle issue during Week 3 prep and drew the questionable tag after logging back-to-back limited practices Thursday and Friday. He's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday and will start opposite Asante Samuel at outside cornerback. Dean has eight tackles (five solo) through the first two games of the regular season.

injuries.shortComment: Porter (conditioning) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Porter had the conditioning label next to his questionable tag for Sunday's AFC North tilt after being limited in practice all week, but he won't make his 2026 regular-season debut Sunday. Asante Samuel will continue to start opposite Jamel Dean at outside cornerback in Porter's absence. Porter's next opportunity to play is Thursday against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Heidenreich (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: It looked like the rookie seventh-rounder was in line for a slightly larger role Sunday after Rico Dowdle (toe) was ruled out. However, Heidenreich will be a healthy scratch for the first time this season, with Travis Homer and Lew Nichols providing depth in the backfield for Jaylen Warren while fellow rookie Kaden Wetjen operates as the primary returner on kickoffs. Heidenreich's next chance to play is Thursday against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Pittman (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
injuries.longComment: The foot injury resulted in Pittman being a limited practice participant throughout the week and taking a questionable tag into Sunday, but the wideout appears to have avoided any setbacks and shouldn't face any major restrictions with his snap count in his return from a one-game absence. With Pittman back in the fold, Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard are both likely to see their playing time take hits.

injuries.shortComment: Hoffman will start at right guard against the Bengals on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: Hoffman operated in a depth role through the first two regular-season games, but he'll work with the first-team offense Sunday as the Steelers overhaul the right side of the offensive line, with Max Iheanachor starting at right tackle. Spencer Anderson and Dylan Cook will be the depth options behind Hoffman and Iheanachor for Week 3.

injuries.shortComment: Iheanachor will start at right tackle against the Bengals on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: Iheanachor played a total of four offensive snaps through the first two games of the regular season while serving as a depth option, but the rookie first-rounder will be a starter Sunday for the first time in his short NFL career. The Steelers are overhauling their entire right side of the offensive line, with Brock Hoffman getting the nod at right guard next to Iheanachor.

injuries.shortComment: The Steelers placed Dunker (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injuries.longComment: Dunker suffered an MCL sprain during Week 3 prep and will need to miss 4-to-6 weeks with the issue. Now on IR, Dunker will need to wait four games before becoming eligible to return to the Steelers' active roster.

injuries.shortComment: The Steelers elevated Nichols from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Nichols has played in one NFL regular-season game, logging six special-teams snaps in the Steelers' Week 9 game against the Colts in 2025. The running back has been elevated to provide additional depth, as Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is questionable to suit up and Rico Dowdle (toe) is already ruled out ahead of Sunday's contest with the Bengals.

injuries.shortComment: The Steelers signed Homer from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Homer was elevated for the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the Patriots, playing two offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the game while logging two rushes for 16 yards. The running back could be the primary option for the Steelers in the Week 3 contest against the Bengals. Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is listed as questionable and Rico Dowdle (toe) has been ruled out, meaning at worst Homer will be the No. 2 or No. 3 option Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Queen recorded two tackles (zero solo) and an interception in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Queen played all 55 defensive snaps against New England but was mostly held off the stat sheet aside from his interception of Drake Maye on the opening drive of the third quarter with the Steelers trailing 10-3. It was the fifth interception of Queen's career and his first since Week 16 of the 2023 campaign. Through two games this season, Queen has logged 10 tackles (two solo) and the pick on one pass breakup.

injuries.shortComment: Washington caught one of his two targets for seven yards in Sunday's loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Washington played 37 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps as the tight end started alongside Pat Freiermuth. The 25-year-old has become a staple of the Steelers' 12-personnel offense and is slated to continue primarily serving as a blocker who sees occasional opportunities in the passing game.

injuries.shortComment: Freiermuth caught four passes (on five targets) for 32 yards while logging a two-yard carry during the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Freiermuth and Darnell Washington were both named starters for Sunday's game, with the former leading all Steelers tight ends with 46 of 67 offensive snaps (68.7 percent). Unlike Week 1 against the Falcons, Freiermuth did not draw a red-zone target from Aaron Rodgers in Week 2, with the veteran quarterback averaging just 4.8 yards per pass attempt against New England. Freiermuth will take a 9-78-1 line (on 10 targets) into a Week 3 AFC North divisional showdown against the Bengals.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson caught five of six targets for 28 yards during the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Wilson stepped into the WR2 role alongside DK Metcalf for Sunday's game due to the absence of Michael Pittman (foot). Wilson responded by leading all Pittsburgh pass catchers in receptions, though he averaged only 5.6 yards per catch in a game where Aaron Rodgers averaged only 4.8 yards per pass attempt. Wilson played 55 of 70 offensive snaps in Week 2, which was tied with rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard for second-most among Steelers wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (68). The Steelers will return home for a Week 3 clash against the Bengals, and Wilson and Bernard would both retain their elevated roles if Pittman is not cleared to return.

injuries.shortComment: Bernard caught four passes on eight targets for 35 yards during the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The rookie second-rounder operated as the WR3 due to the absence of Michael Pittman (foot). Aaron Rodgers struggled at Gillette Stadium, but Bernard did his part by leading the Steelers pass catchers in receiving yards while finishing second in catches behind Roman Wilson (five) and second in targets to DK Metcalf (nine). Pittman's status for Week 3 against the Bengals on Sept. 27 is up in the air, but even if he was ruled out, Bernard's production (along with the other Steelers pass catchers) will be capped unless Rodgers improves his play.

injuries.shortComment: Fautanu (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Fautanu drew the questionable tag for Week 2 after posting a DNP/LP/FP practice log. The third-year pro was cleared to play after going through pregame warmups and will once again start at left tackle.

injuries.shortComment: McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 75 yards and a touchdown while bringing in four of five targets for 41 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: McCaffrey's carry total was modest by his standards, but he still outpaced backup Kaelon Black by 11 carries and four targets while also recording a one-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter. McCaffrey was highly efficient with his rushing opportunities, and he finished second in receptions and third in targets for the 49ers on the afternoon. San Francisco's pass-catching corps suffered further attrition this weekend -- Mike Evans exited the game with rib and oblique injuries, while Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Saturday -- so McCaffrey could continue to see his pass-game work creep up in a Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Evans has a rib/oblique injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed after Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Evans was ruled out of the game due to a rib injury after absorbing a big hit, but it sounds like the veteran wide receiver is also dealing with an oblique injury. Further clarification on Evans' status will surface before the 3-0 49ers host the Broncos in Week 4.

injuries.shortComment: Greenlaw (quadriceps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Greenlaw sustained the injury early in the fourth quarter, and he's been off the field being monitored by training staff since his exit. Garrett Wallow is in the game at weakside linebacker in Greenlaw's absence.

injuries.shortComment: Green (head) has returned to Sunday's game against the 49ers, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
injuries.longComment: Green was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion after taking a hit to the head. He has been cleared by trainers to return and is back on the field for the fourth quarter.

injuries.shortComment: Halton (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Arizona, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
injuries.longComment: Halton had to be helped off the field by trainers after sustaining an ankle injury, and he's been taken to the locker room for further evaluation. Naquan Jones, Kevin Givens and Sebastian Valdez are all in line for more defensive snaps for as long as Halton is out of the game.

injuries.shortComment: Williams (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Williams was carted off the field and into the locker room during the third quarter, so he figures to be closer toward the doubtful side of returning to Sunday's contest. Venderian Lowe figures to take over at left tackle in Williams' absence.

injuries.shortComment: Jones (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Jones sustained a foot injury in the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Dolphins, but the fifth-year pro has been cleared to play in Sunday's NFC West showdown. He's logged three pass defenses and zero tackles through the first two games of the regular season while serving in a rotational role in the secondary.

injuries.shortComment: The 49ers placed Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Robinson was carted off the field due to a right ankle injury during San Francisco's Week 2 win against the Dolphins, after which coach Kyle Shanahan relayed that the wide receiver likely suffered a high-ankle sprain. On Monday, Shanahan said that Robinson was facing a recovery timeline of 3-to-6 weeks, so this move to injured reserve doesn't come as a surprise. Robinson will be first eligible to return to action Sunday, Oct. 25 in Atlanta, but with all of Christian Kirk (calf), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee) and Robinson on IR, the 49ers will be going with Mike Evans (hip), Deebo Samuel, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge at wide receiver this Sunday against the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: The 49ers signed Jones to the active roster Wednesday from the Vikings' practice squad.
injuries.longComment: Jones dealt with an undisclosed injury through the end of training camp and into his tenure with the Vikings' practice squad. The defensive tackle is evidently healthy and set to suit up for the 49ers in Sunday's contest against the Cardinals. Defensive tackle CJ West (undisclosed) was moved to IR in a corresponding move.

injuries.shortComment: The 49ers placed West (undisclosed) on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: It remains unclear what issue is sidelining the second-year player. West will now need to miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the active roster. The defensive tackle has logged five tackles (one solo) over 49 defensive snaps in the 49ers' first two regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Jones did not attempt a pass and lost two yards on two end-of-game kneel-down plays during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: The 49ers had no trouble building a comfortable lead throughout the contest, leading to Jones coming in to mop up over the final two series. The 28-year-old is coming off a sound 2025 campaign, throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions while completing a career-best 69.6 percent of his attempts. While Jones is considered one of the better backup quarterbacks in the NFL, his fantasy ceiling is virtually non-existent as long as Brock Purdy is healthy.

injuries.shortComment: Juszczyk recorded two catches on two targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Juszczyk madę the start and played just over 50 percent of the offensive snaps. The 35-year-old veteran is in his 14th NFL season but doesn't carry much, if any, fantasy value in redraft formats as a lead blocker.

injuries.shortComment: Warner recorded five tackles (one solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a forced fumble during Sunday's 35-13 win versus the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Warner's tackle total was down from Week 1 (11), but he punched a football out of a runner's hands for the second straight week and made a mark in the sack column. He'll be hoping to cause more chaos in a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Brown recorded 13 tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 35-13 win versus the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Most of the small amount of success Miami's offense found against San Francisco in Week 2 came through the air, funneling a healthy number of tackle opportunities to Brown. He'll be looking to lock the defensive secondary back down in Week 3 versus the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Sigle recorded seven tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 35-13 win versus the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Sigle followed up a strong performance in Week 1 with another good game in Week 2, and he has now logged six-plus tackles in all of his last four games going back to last postseason. He has probably played himself into IDP consideration in some formats going into a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: James saw four carries for 15 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: James saw eight offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in the contest. All of the running back's carries came in the final seven minutes of the fourth quarter when the game was all but over.

injuries.shortComment: Pineiro did not have any field-goal tries but converted on all five of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 35-13 win versus the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: In a game where Miami's defense was picked apart by quarterback Brock Purdy, Pineiro's services were barely needed. San Francisco is off to a scorching start in 2026, and there's not much reason to think the Cardinals defense will be the one to slow the momentum Week 3.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Sunday that he's not viewing Aiyuk as an option for the 49ers while the club contends with multiple injuries at receiver, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: After undergoing surgery in October 2024 to address ACL and MCL tears in his right knee, Aiyuk is likely fully healthy at this point, but the mercurial wideout appears to have worn out his welcome with the 49ers. General manager John Lynch said in January that Aiyuk had played his last snap with the franchise, and little on that front appears to have changed in the ensuing months. The 49ers still hold the 28-year-old's rights after placing him on the reserve/left squad list last December, and he's already had his $26.66 million salary for 2026 voided since he failed to attend mandatory rehab sessions and meetings. In order to force his release from the 49ers, Aiyuk will need to formally apply for reinstatement with the league, but he indicated in a July 7 story on his personal Instagram account that he has no plans to immediately do so, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com.

injuries.shortComment: Price carried the ball five times for 15 yards and caught one of three targets for seven yards in Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: The Seahawks' running game continues to struggle, and Price's inability to make a consistent impact is causing him to lose touches. After seeing double-digit carries in each of his first two NFL games, the rookie's six touches trailed both Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three totes and five catches). The chest injury Price suffered in Week 2 may have played a role in that distribution, but he hadn't topped 60 scrimmage yards or found the end zone in either of the first two weeks. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting closer to his 2026 debut, time may be running out for Price to establish himself in the lead role before the backfield gets even more crowded. He'll try to get going in a Week 4 home tilt against the Chargers.

injuries.shortComment: Smith-Njigba caught 10 of 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Having Sam Darnold back under center instead of Drew Lock did nothing to slow Smith-Njigba's momentum. The superstar wideout recorded his third straight game with more than 120 receiving yards while hauling in his fifth and sixth TDs of the season, catching a one-yard toss in the second quarter and an 11-yard strike in the fourth. Smith-Njigba will take an eye-popping 27-405-6 line on 36 targets into a Week 4 clash at home against the Chargers.

injuries.shortComment: Darnold completed 31 of 45 passes for 379 yards and four touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders. He added five yards on his only carry.
injuries.longComment: Making his return from a Week 1 soft-tissue injury, Darnold put up big numbers against a shaky Washington defense as he connected for two scores with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and one each to Cooper Kupp and Eric Saubert. However, Darnold's two INTs both came in the second half and led directly to 14 points for the Commanders, including a 50-yard pick-six by third-string linebacker Kain Medrano that proved to be the game-winning score. Darnold will look to clean things up in a Week 4 home tilt against the Chargers.

injuries.shortComment: Emmanwori (hamstring) returned to Sunday's game against the Commanders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Emmanwori exited the contest due to a hamstring injury. but he's returned in relatively short order. With Emmanwori back in the equation, Julian Neal, Maxen Hook and Nehemiah Pritchett will likely log fewer snaps the rest of the way.

injuries.shortComment: Foster (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Foster will be inactive for the second consecutive week. His next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 4 versus the Chargers.

injuries.shortComment: Milroe (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Washington.
injuries.longComment: Sam Darnold (glute) is available for Sunday's meeting with the Commanders, meaning Drew Lock will move back to the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Despite being inactive for Week 3, Milroe could still see the field if both Darnold and Lock exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: Pili (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Pili drew the questionable tag for Sunday after ending Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited practices. He has not progressed enough in the league's concussion protocol to play against Washington, and his next chance to take the field is Week 4 against the Chargers on Sunday, Oct. 4. Rylie Mills and Mike Morris are both in line to see a slight bump in defensive snaps due to Pili's absence.
